ABOUT · WHY PROPERTICHAIN?

Large assets.
Smaller entry points.

An apartment may exceed one person’s budget, yet access to its value and cash flow can be divided into smaller interests. Propertichain aims to connect existing real estate, evidenced rights and capital from multiple investors on BNB Chain.

01 / ACCESS

Broaden participation in real estate

Rather than funding an entire unit, investors could acquire a smaller interest under an appropriately structured and verified arrangement. Developers gain another route to distributed capital for existing unsold units, while smaller investors gain a way to participate in high-value assets.

USD 1–2 entry is an ambition requiring payment, verification and servicing-cost validation. Small contributions still require an understanding of rights, fees, risks and transfer conditions.

02 / PROPERTY LEVEL

Each property has its own identity and cash flow

Each apartment or shophouse has a unique ID, evidence, token supply and rental vault. Rent is allocated under established ownership and holding-period rules; vacant units generate no rent to distribute.

Property valuation and rental receipts are independent. Daily reference updates are a goal where sufficiently reliable data exists; each record needs a source and timestamp.

03 / PRICE CONTROLS

Reduce manipulation opportunities through rules

Planned controls combine evidence-based valuations, independent review and reconciliation across sources; sellers cannot change prices without the required authority. Unusual-trade alerts, policy limits and trading holds for unsupported prices aim to reduce artificial price moves and FOMO.

Authorized parties may apply scoped pauses or freezes during suspected attacks or abuse, with recorded reasons and reopening conditions. These controls reduce risk; they cannot guarantee the elimination of manipulation or real-world price volatility.

04 / EVIDENCE

Bring real assets onchain responsibly

Owners, developers, banks, operators and appraisers perform real-world work. Authorized parties attest with evidence. Smart contracts check prerequisites before executing permitted actions and recording an audit trail.

Token rights require an effective legal structure and supporting records. Blockchain holds appropriate references, attestations and history; private documents remain offchain under access controls.

FROM WORKFLOW TO IMPACT

More transparency. Less repeated work. Clearer verification.

Standardized records and approvals let parties track a consistent data version. Automating approved steps may shorten reconciliation, reduce repeated entry and limit rental-distribution errors. Actual speed and cost improvements must be measured during the pilot; legal, banking and appraisal work still needs real-world completion.

Potential contribution to BNB Chain

More real-world utility

Property-specific rights, eligible transfers, rental distributions and operational traceability create uses tied to existing assets. No platform altcoin is issued to attract users with rewards.

A broader user base and capital flows

If deployed and widely adopted, the model could bring more developers, operators and smaller investors to BNB Chain, supporting transactions for real needs and capital circulation. Liquidity depends on buyers, sellers, legal conditions and trading mechanisms; tokenization alone does not ensure a buyer or exit.

Rollout path: existing unsold developer inventory → iterative pilot testing, fixes and improvement → internal group rollout → solutions for other developers. Grand Park remains an independent case study; no Vingroup/Vinhomes partnership is confirmed. These impacts are design goals, not achieved results.

TWO WEB3 ENGINEERING PILLARS · PROPOSED DESIGN

Synchronize asset states.
Connect rights and settlement.

Propertichain aims to enforce rights using property-specific evidence: authorized real-world attestations determine which blockchain actions are permitted. These pillars require code and pilot validation; they are not deployed onchain features or claims of exclusive technical novelty.

PILLAR 1 / STATE-DEPENDENT RIGHTS

Tokens governed by each property’s conditions

Each property has a living record of ownership, encumbrances, lease status, sale availability and incidents. Attestations bind the property ID, record version, permission scope, signer and expiry, and may be revoked. Contracts check them before issuance, transfer or rent distribution.

Separate rights rather than freezing everything: an expired valuation may block new trades requiring a valid price while funded rent continues under its own conditions. A transfer-frozen wallet retains accrued rental rights; other properties and vaults remain isolated.

Mid-period transfers: record entitlements by share and holding time, preserve the seller’s accrued claim and prevent duplicate claims by the buyer. Pay only when actual funds are available.

PILLAR 2 / ASSET-BASED SETTLEMENT

From ownership interests to rental obligations

Three planned flows: buy property tokens with crypto; pay rent with crypto; use property A ownership tokens to pay property B rent. Prioritize stablecoins for the MVP; ownership-token settlement follows in the pilot.

Who accepts the tokens? A landlord may explicitly accept them at an agreed valuation, or a buyer may acquire them so the landlord receives stablecoins. Acceptance and conversion liquidity must never be assumed.

Conditional settlement: check transfer permissions, current price, limits and recipient eligibility; preserve accrued rent; transfer assets and discharge the rental obligation atomically where fully onchain. Failure reverts both. Offchain legs need separate conditional holding and reconciliation.

Example: 50 property A tokens settle USD 500 of property B rent

Assume both parties accept USD 10 per token in this simulation. Before transferring 50 A tokens, record the payer’s accrued rental rights and verify attestations and recipient eligibility. Mark the correct B rental period paid only when the asset transfer succeeds. The payer must not lose tokens while the same rental obligation remains outstanding.

Received tokens are not cash: if property B’s landlord/vault receives A tokens, record the asset separately. Parties must pre-agree on in-kind distribution or conversion into stablecoins before cash distribution. Do not report it as cash rent already funded in the vault.

What the technical demo must prove

One property → multiple attestations → conditional issuance → mid-period transfer → correct rental allocation → incident and scoped freeze → approved recovery. Add two simulated properties to test asset-for-rent settlement, including failure cases.

No contracts, wallet connections or actual payments are deployed. Real-world crypto/ownership-token settlement depends on the legal structure, asset conditions, party consent and permitted payment arrangements.
